description: The Dubai Virtual Reference Station (DVRS) is the GNSS reference network of the Survey Department of Dubai Municipality, which the page says was the first virtual reference station system in the Middle East when it was set up in 2003. It has more than 18 GNSS stations covering the whole of Dubai that collect GPS, GLONASS, Galileo and BeiDou signals, and the data is processed with software such as Geo++ and Pivot. It gives instant access to high-accuracy positions for surveying, construction, GIS and positioning applications, with sub-centimetre accuracy, 24 hours a day. The page sits beside the department's geodesy, hydrography and visibility survey services. Access terms, prices and any licence are not given on the page read, so access is arranged through Dubai Municipality. Caveats: the page is short and does not list station coordinates, data formats or archive options, and the English page notes that some content has no translation. Coverage is the Emirate of Dubai. It supports positioning infrastructure studies for construction and utilities, and space weather effects on GNSS; related records are PositioNZ of New Zealand and CROPOS of Croatia.
